candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7: prioritize care based on acuity; participate in quality improvement; utilize resources to promote quality care; organize workload to manage time effectively; practice and advocate for quality and cost-effective care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — staffing, workload, resource use and patient safety
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize inadequate RN staffing as a patient-safety risk associated with missed nursing care and adverse patient outcomes while interpreting staffing evidence with appropriate causal caution.

options.A: Assume lower RN staffing improves safety because fewer nurses reduce handoffs and therefore consistently decrease communication-related errors.
options.B: Recognize inadequate or lower RN staffing as a patient-safety risk associated in observational evidence with missed care, adverse outcomes, and higher mortality.
options.C: Assume staffing does not influence patient outcomes when the number of occupied beds stays constant across the shift.
options.D: Treat RN staffing only as a financial issue because clinical evidence has not linked workload or staffing with patient-safety outcomes.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ PSNet summarizes evidence that appropriate nurse staffing is critical to patient safety. Fewer nurses caring for patients is associated with higher mortality; inadequate staffing can lead to missed nursing care and negative outcomes, and missed care is more prevalent with low staffing. Because much of this evidence is observational and the staffing-outcome relationship is complex, the safest wording is an association rather than an absolute causal claim. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Lower/inadequate nurse staffing is associated with missed nursing care and adverse patient-safety outcomes, including higher mortality, although the relationship is complex and much evidence is observational.
candidate.source_document_title: Patient Safety Amid Nursing Workforce Challenges
candidate.source_locator: Introduction: appropriate nurse staffing is critical to patient safety; fewer nurses are associated with higher patient mortality. Nursing Workforce Challenges and Patient Safety: inadequate staffing can lead to missed care and negative outcomes; missed care is more prevalent with low staffing; appropriate staffing tends to reduce avoidable harm.
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ), Patient Safety Network (PSNet)
candidate.stem: A nurse manager evaluates whether reducing registered-nurse staffing could affect patient safety. Which conclusion is most consistent with the evidence base?
